ζαβουλων.def: of Hebrew origin (H2074); Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of Palestine. KJV: Zabulon.

ζακχαιοσ.def: of Hebrew origin (compare H2140); Zacchæus, an Israelite. KJV: Zacchæus.

ζαρα.def: of Hebrew origin (H2226); Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite. KJV: Zara.

ζαχαριασ.def: of Hebrew origin (H2148); Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two Israelites. KJV: Zacharias.

ζαω.def: a primary verb; to live (literally or figuratively). KJV: life(-time), (a-)live(-ly), quick.

ζεβεδαιοσ.def: of Hebrew origin (compare H2067); Zebedæus, an Israelite. KJV: Zebedee.

ζεστοσ.def: from ζέω (G2204); boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively, fervent). KJV: hot.

ζευγοσ.def: from the same as ζυγός (G2218); a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together) or brace (of birds tied together). KJV: yoke, pair.

ζευκτηρια.def: feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as ζυγός (G2218); a fastening (tiller-rope). KJV: band.

ζευσ.def: of uncertain affinity; in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name Δίς, which is otherwise obsolete; Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks. KJV: Jupiter.

ζεω.def: a primary verb; to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e. (figuratively) be fervid (earnest). KJV: be fervent.

ζηλοσ.def: from ζέω (G2204); properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice). KJV: emulation, envy(-ing), fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal.

ζηλοω.def: from ζῆλος (G2205); to have warmth of feeling for or against. KJV: affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect).

ζηλωτησ.def: the same as ζηλωτής (G2207); a Zealot, i.e. (specially) partisan for Jewish political independence. KJV: Zelotes.

ζημια.def: probably akin to the base of δαμάζω (G1150) (through the idea of violence); detriment. KJV: damage, loss.

ζημιοω.def: from ζημία (G2209); to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience detriment. KJV: be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss.

ζηνασ.def: probably contracted from a poetic form of Ζεύς (G2203) and δῶρον (G1435); Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian. KJV: Zenas.

ζητεω.def: of uncertain affinity; to seek (literally or figuratively); specially, (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against life). KJV: be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X will) seek (after, for, means).

ζητημα.def: from ζητέω (G2212); a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate. KJV: question.

ζητησισ.def: from ζητέω (G2212); a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its theme. KJV: question.

ζιζανιον.def: of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain. KJV: tares.

ζοροβαβελ.def: of Hebrew origin (H2216); Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite. KJV: Zorobabel.

ζοφοσ.def: akin to the base of νέφος (G3509); gloom (as shrouding like a cloud). KJV: blackness, darkness, mist.

ζυγοσ.def: from the root of ζεύγνυμι (to join, especially by a "yoke"); a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales). KJV: pair of balances, yoke.

ζυμη.def: probably from ζέω (G2204); ferment (as if boiling up). KJV: leaven.

ζυμοω.def: from ζύμη (G2219); to cause to ferment. KJV: leaven.

ζωγρεω.def: from the same as ζῶον (G2226) and ἀγρεύω (G64); to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare. KJV: take captive, catch.

ζωη.def: from ζάω (G2198); life (literally or figuratively). KJV: life(-time).

ζωνη.def: probably akin to the base of ζυγός (G2218); a belt; by implication, a pocket. KJV: girdle, purse.

ζωννυμι.def: from ζώνη (G2223); to bind about (especially with a belt). KJV: gird.

ζωογονεω.def: from the same as ζῶον (G2226) and a derivative of γίνομαι (G1096); to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death. KJV: live, preserve.

ζωον.def: neuter of a derivative of ζάω (G2198); a live thing, i.e. an animal. KJV: beast.

ζωοποιεω.def: from the same as ζῶον (G2226) and ποιέω (G4160); to (re-)vitalize (literally or figuratively). KJV: make alive, give life, quicken.
